text: An access entry of SCR-46 carries the screen id, one object-type value of the agent monitor, the agent codes on screen, the segment (the product group and the region of the case at run time), the date range, the caller reference, the outcome and the time; the object type is one value of a list in force named AGENT_MONITOR in this document, and the log read takes objectType, agent, segment, from, to, page and size with page bounds as parameter rows. No metric value, agent output, prompt text or personal field is part of the entry.
why: The legacy story names no field of an access entry, the TSD gives API-P4-008 no parameter list and the FSD describes the event in prose only. The story still has to record what a reviewer needs to answer 'who watched which agent and when', so the minimum set is fixed here and marked with the placeholder; the object type is a list value and not a code constant, so a different code is a data change.

text: The access event of a read is one entry of the service's local decision-record chain written through the DP-03 library, under the library's own record code for an access event; the code is taken from the library's code set at build time and is never written as a business constant in this story. The entry is appended in the transaction window of the read it describes, and the entry is what the access-log read projects.
why: FEAT-ACA-08 puts the access log into the append-only decision log, and DP-03 makes that log local with the central ledger in rwb-decision. No source names the record code of an access event or of a refusal, and inventing one would be a business value; the code set is the library's, so the story names no value and carries the placeholder.

text: The agent monitor keeps two gates: the screen route asks rwb-access for Platform administration R before any metric row is asked, as the legacy story fixes, and the metric read keeps Rules and parameters R at rwb-agent as its contract fixes. A caller needs both to see a measure, a refusal of either answers 403 with MSG-P4-002, and this story neither changes the agent contract nor merges the two letters into one.
why: The two sources are both current and neither is superseded: the legacy story is the business intent and the agent contract is the published interface. R-PREC would put the technical specification above the story, but the agent slice has already resolved its own read to Rules and parameters R and left the legacy right recorded. Changing the agent contract from this slice would be an edit of another service's contract in a Work Package that does not carry it, so the two are kept and the disagreement is recorded.

text: A read of SCR-46 whose access entry or refusal entry cannot be appended is not served: the route answers 503 with MSG-P7-003 and no metric row reaches the screen. The event is written in the request and not by a job, a retry or a reconciliation step, so there is no path in which a read happens and is recorded later.
why: REQ-ACA-006 says every access event is written, and the FSD exception pattern of the module withholds the answer when the record cannot be written (the personal-data read shows the masked value and the message instead of the clear one). A read that is served without its record would break the control the story exists for, so the fail-closed reading is the only one consistent with the requirement.

impact: If the service is to serve the read and alert on the missing record instead, BR3, AC3 and the 503 row of section 5 change and the control becomes a monitoring control rather than an inline one.

text: DP-15 is met by one step in the service's own Flyway sequence that adds a read index on the local record table (object type, agent code and business date) and seeds the agent-monitor value of the object-type list. The step adds no table and no column: the entry is held by the DP-03 library's table, and the object type is a value of a list in force. The accept date and the version number are left to the sequence in force.
why: The legacy migration V10_007 adds the segment columns of agent_run, which are rwb-agent's, so the legacy marker cannot be carried over as it stands. The access-log read over a period and an agent needs an index on the record table; adding a table for the object set would put a second record beside the append-only chain, which DP-03 forbids in practice.
